header: For five years, AKA was a research studio working on decentralized identity. Then the AI era gave the company a new direction, and it needed a teaser site to reflect it. I designed and built the site from scratch.

summary.team: Me, plus aka engineers on browser support

layout.title: Background
text: Before a launch, no one knows what you do. That curiosity is one of the few advantages a startup has, and it doesn’t last. I created the teaser site to lean into it.

At the time, Twitter was full of people using OpenClaw to automate their lives, and seeing databases get deleted by agents in the process. It was a real problem, and everyone building with agents had felt it. And aka was building an AI-first identity product to help solve it.
So the concept was to show, loosely, what it looks like when agents run wild. The whole site builds tension, and the only way to release it is to enter your email.

layout.title: Under the hood
text: With Claude Code as my daily driver, I built the site in React and Three.js, rendering with WebGPU and custom shaders for the cords’ materials. For the physics of the cords (the bounce, the weight), I used Rapier, a JavaScript physics engine.
Everything was built in full 3D, then locked in place in a 2D view for the user.

media.name: three_experiments.mp4
media.title: A few of the dozen-plus experiments before the final site

text: To make precise adjustments along the way, I built a control panel on top of the scene. Its sliders let me shape the cords, tune the physics, and move the camera, all in real time.

layout.title: Result
text: The relaunch went great. Within a few weeks, hundreds of people had joined aka’s waitlist.

Before AI, a site like this required an agency, or weeks of rounds with a developer. Now I could design directly in code. And the control panel I built let me adjust the cords, physics, and camera right in the browser and see every change instantly.
